stance: Agent identity is fragmenting into a tactical split between immediate, operator-published IP and user-agent lists and longer-term standards for privacy-preserving, conduct-based cryptographic verification.
adoption_shape: While commercial operators like Amazon maintain control through practical, bilateral mechanisms by publishing dedicated IP ranges and distinct user-agent strings for search bots and live fetchers, standardizers in the IETF Web Bot Auth Working Group are simultaneously constructing multi-tiered protocols to decouple behavioral verification from operator identity.
new_entrants: Specification authors McKenna and Suresh have introduced drafts into the IETF to standardize reporting mechanisms for authentication results and tiered attestation models aimed at preserving anonymity during data collection.
watch_for: Whether large-scale crawler operators adopt the IETF's standardized verification outcome reporting mechanisms or continue relying exclusively on self-hosted IP lists and user-agent declarations.
